subject: MedSecure — transactional log pruning & attestation plan (SIG follow-up)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@medsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medsecure.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up — request for transactional log pruning plan and attestation

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. MedSecure's compliance team reviewed the SIG/CAIQ responses and we have one outstanding ask before we can proceed to procurement: confirmation and evidence that Redwood can support a customer-specific transactional log pruning policy.

Constraints from our side:
- We need transactional request logs (transaction IDs, timestamps, routing metadata) retained for 45 days rather than the standard 90 days, due to our internal data minimization policy tied to patient-identifiable workflows.
- During a legal hold we need the ability to freeze deletions for a 30-day window for affected tenants and to obtain an export of the exact audit trail.
- We also need an attestation we can present to our auditors (SIG/SOC2-style language) that covers deletion proof, retention tags, and where applicable, proof-of-delete artifacts.

Can you send a short plan that describes: scope (which logs would be pruned/kept), automated enforcement (how pruning is scheduled), evidence artifacts (what you can provide to auditors), and an expected timeline to produce the attestation? If you can include sample evidence files or a template attestation, that would speed our review.

I've attached our redlined SIG extract for context (MedSecure_SIG.pdf). Alex Peters from Engineering is copied for any technical clarifications.

Appreciate a response this week if possible — procurement is on a tight calendar.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Director, Compliance
MedSecure Health

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — request for transactional log pruning plan and attestation

Hi Samira,

Thanks — we can support a tenant-scoped retention variance, but I want to make sure we answer your auditables precisely. Quick clarifying questions before we draft the plan:

1) When you say "transactional request logs" can you confirm whether you mean both (a) application-level request logs we ingest (API request/response metadata) and (b) internal system traces / worker logs? We typically treat those differently for retention.
2) For legal holds, do you expect Redwood to preserve a full copy in our control plane (Redwood-managed) or is customer-side export during the hold acceptable?
3) Any regulatory constraints we should account for beyond your internal policy (e.g., state-level health records rules)?

I'll loop in Jonas (security/infra) to outline the technical enforcement and evidence artifacts. Ben — can you weigh in on contract language and timeline for the attestation?

I'll assemble a preliminary mutual action plan and a sample attestation (MA-Prelim-MAP.docx) and circulate by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@medsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alex Peters <alex.peters@medsecure.com>
Date: 2027-03-19T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — transactional log pruning & attestation (technical plan)

Hi all,

Thanks for the context. High-level summary of how we can meet the 45-day retention + legal-hold requirement and the types of evidence we can deliver:

Scope
- "Transactional request logs" = application API request metadata and routing headers stored in our request telemetry index. Worker/system traces are out of scope for the 45-day carve-out unless explicitly included by request (we can scope them but they are normally retained per infra rules).

Enforcement mechanics
- Tenant-scoped retention tags: we will add a tenant-level retention policy flag (retention_days=45) that overrides the default 90-day TTL for the request-telemetry index.
- Deletion pipeline: deletions are carried out by a time-based garbage-collector job (kafka -> coldstore lifecycle) that marks keys for deletion and then issues a secure erase call to object storage. The process records a deletion token and SHA256 deletion seal stored in our immutability audit store (read-only) for  +12 months for attestation purposes.
- Legal hold: when a legal hold is applied to a tenant ID, the GC job skips the affected keys and marks them as "hold:true"; we can also produce a zipped export of the relevant audit trail and object references for a requested timeframe.

Evidence artifacts we can provide
- Retention policy matrix (per-tenant values): kafka-retention-matrix.csv
- Deletion playbook and pseudo-audit output template: deletion-playbook.md
- Example proof-of-delete artifact (deletion token + seal example) — we provide a signed JSON blob and timestamped signature from our HSM.
- Sample attestation wording that maps to SIG/SOC2 categories (we'll draft this in the MA doc).

Operational controls / timeline
- Implementation of tenant flag + matrix change: 3 business days (config + test in our staging cluster).
- Evidence package and signed attestation: 5–7 business days (includes security review and legal sign-off).

Risks / items to confirm
- If MedSecure requires system traces included, ETA extends by ~5 business days due to sampling and storage differences.
- For exports during a legal hold we need a signed Data Export Agreement (DE-Addendum) to ensure we can transfer the audit bundle securely.

I'm attaching the retention matrix and deletion playbook for your review. If this looks good I'll coordinate the staging test and produce the formal attestation artifact.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — transactional log pruning & attestation plan

Jonas / Marissa,

This is exactly the level of detail we needed — thank you. A few quick asks to close the loop:

1) Please include in the attestation language an explicit statement that deletion seals and signed JSON blobs will be retained for at least 12 months after deletion and the signing key was generated by an HSM (or equivalent).
2) We need confirmation that the legal hold export will include the raw object references + the integrity seals so our auditors can verify provenance.
3) Can Redwood commit to the 5–7 business day turnaround for the signed attestation once the tenant flag is set in staging? Procurement will accept that timeline pending the DE-Addendum; Legal Ops will send the addendum to Ben.

If you can drop the final attestation and sample proof artifacts in the HubSpot record linked here (HS-89321) and route DocuSign to me, we can finalize SOW review this week.

One more note — we're happy to accept the 45-day retention window for transactional logs and keep system traces out of scope for now.

Regards,
Samira Khan
Director, Compliance
MedSecure Health
